To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). # Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Harbourglass Ventures "Seller Update" draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

---

## Preliminary point: the Seller's framing should not be accepted

The cover material asks us to treat every **[STANDARD]** clause as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to look only at **[OPEN]** items. It also says the package is "FINAL" and was "settled at principal level."

- **No clause in the package is marked [OPEN].** Following the note would mean reviewing nothing.
- **There is no record of agreement.** We have no term sheet, signed heads, or principal-level correspondence confirming these positions. The labels are the Seller's own.
- **The "market context" preamble is advocacy.** Some points (for example a cap of 10–20%) are within a negotiable range. Others are not usual buyer-accepted terms in Australian practice: constructive buyer-knowledge bars, general data-room disclosure against all warranties, and title warranties capped alongside general warranties.

**Recommendation:** Treat every item as open. Confirm in the cover email to the mark-up that the Buyer has not agreed any of the positions, unless the deal team holds documented agreement I haven't seen.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller position:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) on general Warranty Claims. Because of cl 12.3 and cl 13 (see SPA-N-014), it is drafted to extend to *all* Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A cap applying only to general warranty claims, preferably 30–50% (AUD 7.2m–12m) given the known risk profile. Title/capacity, tax, specific indemnities and fraud should sit outside it, with fundamentals capped at 100% of price.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** A 20% cap is tolerable only if every specific indemnity and fundamental warranty is carved out. As drafted, AUD 4.8m would have to absorb Bluefen, Ironquay, the privacy incident and title risk together.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim. AUD 250,000 basket (about 1.04%), *deductible*, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A de minimis of about AUD 10,000–15,000, with related claims aggregated. A **tipping** basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120,000) that, once exceeded, allows recovery from the first dollar. Neither threshold should apply to indemnities, tax, title or fraud.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter (tipping basket, related-claims aggregation).** A deductible basket permanently writes off AUD 250k. Without aggregation, related losses such as the three linked Sandbar renewals could be split to fall under the thresholds.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller position:** Claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion, and that limit applies to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** At least 24 months for general warranties, so the period covers two full audit cycles post-Completion. Tax claims should run 5–7 years (the ATO amendment period plus a buffer). Title and capacity claims should run 7 years (above the NSW 6-year contract limitation period). Specific indemnities should run until the underlying matter is resolved and limitation has expired.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter and reverse the default.** The limit should apply only to general warranties *unless stated otherwise*. As drafted, 18 months could bar tax and title claims before they are even discoverable.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties should be capped at 100% of price, excluded from the de minimis and basket, unqualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge, and subject to a 7-year period.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, and recovery capped at AUD 4.8m is not a remedy. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** None. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature," which on their face includes fraud, dishonesty and misleading conduct.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out stating that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision applies to fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful misconduct, wilful concealment, or claims under the ACL/Corporations Act that cannot lawfully be excluded. The carve-out should cover the Seller and its officers, employees and advisers.
- **Recommendation:** **Insert an express carve-out (non-negotiable).** NSW courts are unlikely to enforce limitations against fraud, but silence invites dispute. It also leaves open arguments that "of any nature" ousts misleading-conduct claims.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Sch 7 / Disclosure Letter cl 1)
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room "as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026," the Accounts, statutory registers and *all* publicly searchable records.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, made "fairly, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter."
  - No general data-room disclosure, or at most disclosure of identified documents rather than everything "referred to" in them.
  - Public records limited to named ASIC and PPSR searches on a stated date.
  - No disclosure at all against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 1.1–1.2 general disclosure.** As drafted, the Seller could defeat almost any warranty claim by pointing to a document buried in DD-002 to DD-012. Clause 1.4 (non-admission) can stay.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is constructive knowledge.
- **Buyer should want:** Deletion, plus an express pro-sandbagging clause: buyer knowledge, investigation or due diligence does not reduce warranty or indemnity claims. If compromise is needed, limit it to the *actual* knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, and exclude advisers and fundamental, tax and indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete and replace with a pro-sandbagging clause.** Every issue in this review was found in diligence. This clause would extinguish exactly the claims the indemnities are meant to protect.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller position:** "Addressed." Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered. Disclosure Letter item 2 confirms there is **no** final consent and **no** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A condition precedent requiring an unconditional written consent from Bluefen, on terms satisfactory to the Buyer, with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen.
  - The condition to be waivable by the Buyer only.
  - A Buyer right to terminate if it is not satisfied by the End Date.
  - Disclosure of any amended terms Bluefen seeks as a price of consent.
- **Recommendation:** **Tighten the condition precedent and remove the Seller's deemed satisfaction.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of revenue. A consent that is delivered but still conditional, or a lost contract, would materially undermine the valuation.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller position:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion." The facility has not been repaid and no discharge has been provided (DL item 3). The change-control at cl 8.1 is triggered by the sale.
- **Buyer should want:** The facility treated as Debt and deducted from price, or repaid from the purchase price through the funds flow at Completion. The following should be **Completion deliverables**:
  - an executed payoff letter;
  - a deed of release;
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within a short fixed period;
  - return of any title documents.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-Completion release.** The deal is debt-free, so Riverlark must be cleared at Completion. Riverlark security may also extend over the shares or assets being acquired, which bears on title (see SPA-N-015).

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller position:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses described as "a matter for the Seller" and left out of the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed (DL item 5).
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses plus all employer on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee where applicable, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation) treated as Transaction Costs or Debt. They should be deducted from price or paid through Company payroll from Seller-funded amounts at Completion. A specific indemnity should cover any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** **Itemise in the funds flow and deduct.** The liability sits with the Company, so a Seller "matter" left off the funds flow becomes a Buyer cost of AUD 420k plus on-costs after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000 open per DD-010). DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room (DL item 4).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **Completion deliverable or condition precedent**: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, or settlement of the outstanding amount from price.
  - A broader specific indemnity covering *all* loss from any Ironquay claim or ownership defect in the SOW3 materials. This includes infringement claims, re-development or replacement costs and business interruption.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers.
- **Recommendation:** **Expand substantially.** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee. The risk is that the Company does not own IP embedded in its product.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6, DD-006)
- **Seller position:** A "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material." About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent by link to an unintended external address. Access, scope and the need to notify are all undetermined.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation and a notifiable data breach assessment under Part IIIC of the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), with Buyer consultation rights.
  - Notification to the OAIC and individuals if required.
  - A specific indemnity, outside all limitations, for regulatory penalties, investigation and notification costs, remediation, third-party and customer claims, and contractual liabilities to the affected customers.
  - Privacy and data warranties that are not qualified by this disclosure.
  - A retention or escrow amount, or W&I-excluded cover funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** **Specific indemnity plus covenant.** The assessment may already be running against the Privacy Act's 30-day expectation. The Seller's "not material" characterisation is unsupported, and its own disclosure says it is unresolved.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller position:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) characterised as "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter does *not* say they are ordinary course, unavoidable, terminable or accrued (DL item 8).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies of all three contracts, with terms, termination rights and timing.
  - Confirmation of whether they were entered or renewed in contemplation of the sale.
  - Any non-ordinary-course or pre-paid-but-unaccrued amounts treated as Debt or Transaction Costs.
  - Aggregation of all three for threshold purposes.
  - A warranty or covenant that no further related renewals are made before Completion without Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept as ordinary course without evidence.** The Seller's cover note contradicts its own Disclosure Letter, and splitting the cost into three AUD 110k pieces looks designed to avoid scrutiny.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13). Limitations and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer should want:** Separate, expressly defined regimes:
  1. general warranties (cap, basket, time limit);
  2. fundamental warranties;
  3. tax warranties and tax indemnity;
  4. specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy incident, bonuses and any others);
  5. fraud.

  General limitations should apply **only** to category 1 unless stated otherwise. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses should be limited accordingly.
- **Recommendation:** **Reverse the default and define categories.** This one drafting device collapses every protection in SPA-N-004, 005, 010, 011, 012 and 016 into the AUD 4.8m, 18-month general regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller position:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register showing Harbourglass holding 100%. DL item 10 concedes this only identifies the source relied on.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification before Completion:
  - a current ASIC company extract matching the register;
  - historic issue and transfer documents;
  - the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emption, drag/tag);
  - confirmation there are no options, convertibles, ESOP or other equity rights;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, with a release of any Riverlark or other security over the shares.

  Completion deliverables should include original certificates, signed transfers and resignations. Title warranties should be fundamental (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation:** **Verify independently; the register is necessary but not sufficient.** A register is prima facie evidence only, and undischarged financier security is a live risk here.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime." No tax indemnity or specific IP terms have been tabled.
- **Buyer should want:** A full tax warranty schedule and a **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion taxes. This should cover income tax, GST, payroll tax and superannuation guarantee charge, including on the DD-005 bonuses. It should come with tax-specific time limits (SPA-N-003), conduct-of-claims provisions, and no general disclosure against it. IP warranties should cover ownership, sufficiency, contractor assignments (Ironquay), open-source use and the absence of infringement.
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as OPEN and table Buyer drafts.** These terms have not been negotiated. Placing them under the general regime by default would cap and time-bar the categories of risk that most commonly surface after Completion.

---

## Other items to note (not in the requested list)
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says only notification is needed, or that no consent is triggered by a share sale. Have the provisions reviewed for change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording, and add notices as Completion deliverables if needed.
- **W&I insurance:** If W&I insurance is contemplated, the known matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) will be excluded from cover. That makes the Seller-backed specific indemnities and a retention more important, not less.

## Suggested mark-up priorities
1. Fraud carve-out, category separation, and fundamental/title regime (SPA-N-005, 014, 004)
2. Delete general disclosure and the buyer-knowledge bar (SPA-N-006, 007)
3. Specific indemnities and Completion deliverables for Ironquay, DD-006, Riverlark and bonuses (SPA-N-009 to 012)
4. Bluefen condition precedent (SPA-N-008)
5. Economic terms: cap, basket, time limits (SPA-N-001 to 003)
6. Tax/IP schedules, Sandbar and title verification (SPA-N-013, 015, 016)

*This review is a working analysis for the Buyer deal team. Final positions should be confirmed by the Buyer's NSW-qualified legal advisers.*

  - A condition precedent requiring an unconditional written consent from Bluefen, on terms satisfactory to the Buyer, with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen.
  - The condition to be waivable by the Buyer only.
  - A Buyer right to terminate if it is not satisfied by the End Date.
  - Disclosure of any amended terms Bluefen seeks as a price of consent.
- **Recommendation:** **Tighten the condition precedent and remove the Seller's deemed satisfaction.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of revenue. A consent that is delivered but still conditional, or a lost contract, would materially undermine the valuation.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller position:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion." The facility has not been repaid and no discharge has been provided (DL item 3). The change-control at cl 8.1 is triggered by the sale.
- **Buyer should want:** The facility treated as Debt and deducted from price, or repaid from the purchase price through the funds flow at Completion. The following should be **Completion deliverables**:
  - an executed payoff letter;
  - a deed of release;
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within a short fixed period;
  - return of any title documents.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-Completion release.** The deal is debt-free, so Riverlark must be cleared at Completion. Riverlark security may also extend over the shares or assets being acquired, which bears on title (see SPA-N-015).

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller position:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses described as "a matter for the Seller" and left out of the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed (DL item 5).
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses plus all employer on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee where applicable, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation) treated as Transaction Costs or Debt. They should be deducted from price or paid through Company payroll from Seller-funded amounts at Completion. A specific indemnity should cover any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** **Itemise in the funds flow and deduct.** The liability sits with the Company, so a Seller "matter" left off the funds flow becomes a Buyer cost of AUD 420k plus on-costs after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000 open per DD-010). DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room (DL item 4).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **Completion deliverable or condition precedent**: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, or settlement of the outstanding amount from price.
  - A broader specific indemnity covering *all* loss from any Ironquay claim or ownership defect in the SOW3 materials. This includes infringement claims, re-development or replacement costs and business interruption.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers.
- **Recommendation:** **Expand substantially.** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee. The risk is that the Company does not own IP embedded in its product.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6, DD-006)
- **Seller position:** A "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material." About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent by link to an unintended external address. Access, scope and the need to notify are all undetermined.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation and a notifiable data breach assessment under Part IIIC of the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), with Buyer consultation rights.
  - Notification to the OAIC and individuals if required.
  - A specific indemnity, outside all limitations, for regulatory penalties, investigation and notification costs, remediation, third-party and customer claims, and contractual liabilities to the affected customers.
  - Privacy and data warranties that are not qualified by this disclosure.
  - A retention or escrow amount, or W&I-excluded cover funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** **Specific indemnity plus covenant.** The assessment may already be running against the Privacy Act's 30-day expectation. The Seller's "not material" characterisation is unsupported, and its own disclosure says it is unresolved.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller position:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) characterised as "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter does *not* say they are ordinary course, unavoidable, terminable or accrued (DL item 8).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies of all three contracts, with terms, termination rights and timing.
  - Confirmation of whether they were entered or renewed in contemplation of the sale.
  - Any non-ordinary-course or pre-paid-but-unaccrued amounts treated as Debt or Transaction Costs.
  - Aggregation of all three for threshold purposes.
  - A warranty or covenant that no further related renewals are made before Completion without Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept as ordinary course without evidence.** The Seller's cover note contradicts its own Disclosure Letter, and splitting the cost into three AUD 110k pieces looks designed to avoid scrutiny.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13). Limitations and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer should want:** Separate, expressly defined regimes:
  1. general warranties (cap, basket, time limit);
  2. fundamental warranties;
  3. tax warranties and tax indemnity;
  4. specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy incident, bonuses and any others);
  5. fraud.

  General limitations should apply **only** to category 1 unless stated otherwise. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses should be limited accordingly.
- **Recommendation:** **Reverse the default and define categories.** This one drafting device collapses every protection in SPA-N-004, 005, 010, 011, 012 and 016 into the AUD 4.8m, 18-month general regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller position:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register showing Harbourglass holding 100%. DL item 10 concedes this only identifies the source relied on.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification before Completion:
  - a current ASIC company extract matching the register;
  - historic issue and transfer documents;
  - the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emption, drag/tag);
  - confirmation there are no options, convertibles, ESOP or other equity rights;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, with a release of any Riverlark or other security over the shares.

  Completion deliverables should include original certificates, signed transfers and resignations. Title warranties should be fundamental (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation:** **Verify independently; the register is necessary but not sufficient.** A register is prima facie evidence only, and undischarged financier security is a live risk here.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime." No tax indemnity or specific IP terms have been tabled.
- **Buyer should want:** A full tax warranty schedule and a **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion taxes. This should cover income tax, GST, payroll tax and superannuation guarantee charge, including on the DD-005 bonuses. It should come with tax-specific time limits (SPA-N-003), conduct-of-claims provisions, and no general disclosure against it. IP warranties should cover ownership, sufficiency, contractor assignments (Ironquay), open-source use and the absence of infringement.
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as OPEN and table Buyer drafts.** These terms have not been negotiated. Placing them under the general regime by default would cap and time-bar the categories of risk that most commonly surface after Completion.
